Gel densitometry

Protein in supernatant: from gel to mg/L

This page turns the darkness of the band of your protein in each gel lane into mg/L of that protein in your supernatant, by comparing it with the same purified protein of known amount run on a gel. Works for IgG, Fab, fusion proteins, nanobodies and others: choose yours below. Everything happens in this browser; nothing is uploaded. Only the intact, monomeric band is measured.

Gels in this session

Which protein are you measuring?

The names and sizes on this page follow your choice. The calculation is the same for every protein: it only compares band darkness with a control gel.

kDa means kilodalton, the unit of protein size. It is used to help you check the right band against your marker lane.

ARecta patró (control gel)

A gel with only purified antibody in a dilution series, loaded twice (1000 → 10.2 ng), plus two mock lanes. Run it once, then repeat it whenever you like: each gel you add is averaged into the recta patró, which makes it more reliable. Choose whether to always use it for new gels.

BNew transfection gel (supernatants)

The gel with the supernatants you want to measure. Put the same two control dilutions in every gel (for example 400 ng and 64 ng, inside the working range of the recta patró): they tell the tool how strongly this gel stained.

No file at hand? Try a simulated one:

Step 1

Check the IgG position

In every lane the tool takes the one band nearest this position and ignores all others; the same rule for control lanes and sample lanes, so every lane is weighed the same way. The position is not fixed: it depends on the gel and the run. The tool reads it from your control lane with the most antibody, where purified IgG is the only strong band. Check it against your marker lane: it should be the ~150 kDa intact IgG. To set it yourself, type a value; to go back to automatic, empty the box. A lane with no band within the window is reported as not detected, never given a neighbouring band.

Size marker: not set yet.

Step 2
Say what is in each lane

  

    
control
purified antibody, give the amount in ng.

    
mock
supernatant from mock transfected cells (should show no band at the IgG position).

    
sample
your supernatant, give the µL you loaded and type a name.

    
ignore
marker lane or anything else.

  

  
If you diluted a supernatant before loading, enter the µL of original supernatant it contains
    (11.25 µL of a 1:2 dilution = 5.6 µL). A lane missing from the file means the iBright found no band there; it is
    treated as not detected.

  

    
  

  
Add a file in box A or B above.







  
Step 3
The curve that links darkness to amount

  
Band darkness grows with the amount of antibody, roughly as darkness = A × ngb.
  The control lanes show where this gel sits on that relationship, because stain and exposure
  change from gel to gel. The more control lanes, the better the curve is known.

  
Waiting for step 2.







  
Step 4
Result

  
Each sample's band darkness is read off the curve to give ng in the lane, then divided by the
  µL loaded: mg/L = ng ÷ µL (1 ng/µL = 1 mg/L). The range is the 95 % uncertainty of the curve and of the
  band. The report under the table says which samples can be called different, using the variability
  measured on your control gel.

  

    

      

        
Variability you accept

        
Lane to lane variability (1 SD, the usual spread of one lane against another). It sets how far apart two samples must be before they are called different.

      

      
auto

Step 5
Global ranking

  
All the gels with samples in this session, ranked together against the same recta patró. Tick or untick a gel in
  the list at the top to include it or not. Two samples on different gels must differ more than two samples on the same
  gel before they are called different, because each gel carries the uncertainty of its own scale. Download the results (CSV) to
  carry on another day: importing that file brings every gel and the recta patró back.

Your gels

  
Gel layouts

  
The raw data file from the iBright has the same format for every gel: it only holds band volumes, not what you loaded.
  So you describe it once, here. A layout says, lane by lane, what each lane is (control with its ng,
  mock, sample with the µL loaded and a name, or ignore). The tool tells control gels from
  transfection gels by the box you use: files added in box A use the layout chosen for control gels, files added in box
  B use the layout chosen for transfection gels. You can still change any lane later in step 2.

Step 1


Size marker: how big is this band?


Tell the tool which marker (the ladder of proteins of known size, in kDa, kilodaltons) you ran, and it turns every position (Rf) on this gel into a size.
It then checks that the band used for your protein has the size you expect, and can place the position in step 1 for you. The marker does not change the mg/L, it is an extra safety check.
You can choose a different marker for every gel.
